_howto: Production Pay tours. steps = page tour. sections = one tour per screen (first visit) plus pop-up form tours (overlay, offered the first time). Guides are in piecework_guides.json. Never reuse a step id.
title: Production Pay tour
whatsNewText: We've added something new here since you last took the tour.

steps.title: Welcome to Production Pay
steps.text:
Pay people for what they produce: set up your farms and units, teams and activities with their rates, give teams tasks, then check each day's production and commit it to payroll.

Use Next and Back, or your arrow keys. Press Esc to close.

steps.title: All Production Pay screens
steps.text: Every screen is listed here. A good order to set up in: Production Settings, Teams, Activities & Pricing, then Tasks.

steps.title: Production Dashboard
steps.text: Today at a glance: production per team and activity, its value, open tasks, days still to commit to payroll, and job costing.

steps.title: Field Maps
steps.text: Where production was captured, on a map of your farms and units.

steps.title: Tasks
steps.text: Give a team or a phone user work to do: which activities, on which farm and units, and the target.

steps.title: Daily Production
steps.text: Check each team's day: quantities captured on the phones, their clockings and pay, then commit it to payroll.

steps.title: Job Costing Timesheet
steps.text: Time people clocked against jobs on the mobile app, with running and flagged jobs.

steps.title: Teams
steps.text: Your production teams, their members and their manager. These are separate from Employee Master's Custom Teams.

steps.title: Activities & Pricing
steps.text: What people are paid for (for example picking, per bin) and the rate for each, with a dated price history.

steps.title: Production Reports
steps.text: Production, pay and job costing reports, for printing or Excel.

steps.title: Production Settings
steps.text: The gear opens Settings: farms and units with their GPS boundaries, and the rules that apply to everyone.

steps.title: Make more room
steps.text: Collapse the menu to icons only, and click again to open it.

steps.title: Refresh Data
steps.text: Reloads everything on this page, for example after phones have synced new production.

steps.title: Search any screen
steps.text: Type what you're looking for, like daily production or pricing, to jump straight to any screen you have access to, in any module.

steps.title: Your menu
steps.text: Click your name for your profile, other areas of the system, Dark Mode and logout.

steps.title: Launchpad
steps.text: Back to your home screen with all your modules.

steps.title: Help & Tours
steps.text: Opens the same help menu as the ? button.

steps.title: Dark Mode
steps.text: Switch between dark and light. Your choice follows your login to any computer.

steps.title: Help is always here
steps.text: Click ? for this tour, a tour of the screen you're on, what's new, and hands-on how-to guides such as setting up farms, creating a team, or adding an activity with its rate.

steps.title: You're all set
steps.text: Each screen also has its own short tour. It starts the first time you open that screen, and you can replay it any time from ?.

steps.title: Which period
steps.text: Pick a period on the left or click a start and an end day on the calendar. The arrows step a whole period back or forward. The chip next to it chooses what to compare with.

steps.title: Today
steps.text: People who captured today and the piece value at worker rates. Your to-do: team-days still to commit to payroll, overdue tasks, and job costing to check. Click any of them to open its screen.

steps.title: This period
steps.text: Piece value, people, entries, job costing hours and tasks completed, each with the change against the compare period. Click one to show it on the chart below.

steps.title: Per day
steps.text: The chosen figure day by day: this period in navy, the compare period dashed in grey before it.

steps.title: Per team
steps.text: Each team in the period: people, entries, piece value and whether it is committed to payroll. Open takes you to that team in Daily Production.

steps.title: Waiting to be committed
steps.text: Every team-day in the last 14 days with production not yet committed to payroll. Click Open to check and commit it.

steps.title: Four sections
steps.text: Farms & Units: where the work happens. Production Rules and Job Costing: rules that apply to everyone. Payroll Periods: periods and locking. Search settings finds a setting by name.

steps.title: Your farms and units
steps.text: One sheet: each farm is a heading row with its units under it. Type over a name or the hectares, or paste rows straight from Excel. The arrow opens and closes a farm.

steps.title: Find, filter, Excel
steps.text: Search finds a farm or unit. Filters: active, inactive, with or without a location. Data Tools: export to Excel, import from Excel (new ones are added, hectares updated), or a blank template.

steps.title: Add a farm
steps.text: + Farm puts a new farm at the top of the sheet with the cursor in its name.

steps.title: Add units
steps.text: The empty line under each farm adds a unit: type the name and hectares and press Enter, and the cursor stays there for the next one. Pasting several lines adds them all.

steps.title: Draw it on the satellite map
steps.text: Opens the satellite map: click dot by dot around the edge, drag a dot to move it, then Done. Give it its own colour. Field Maps shows it, and the phones get its centre and size.

steps.title: Saving
steps.text: Nothing is saved while you type. As soon as something changed, a bar across the top says how many rows; Save first shows what will change, then saves it.

steps.title: Employees in more than one team
steps.text: When on, adding someone to a team keeps them in their other teams. Otherwise they move.

steps.title: Ignore overtime
steps.text: All clocked hours count as normal time, and the overtime columns are hidden in Daily Production. Employee Costs still shows the overtime hours as TNA records them.

steps.title: Deduct piecework hours
steps.text: When on, hours spent on piecework come off normal time. When off, people earn their full normal time as well as their piecework pay.

steps.title: Global Hourly Rate
steps.text: When on, this rate replaces every employee's own hourly rate in Production Pay, from the date you choose: in Daily Production and the wage reports.

steps.title: Saving the rules
steps.text: Nothing in Production Rules or Job Costing applies until you save. As soon as you change something, an Unsaved changes bar shows at the bottom with Save and Discard.

steps.title: Job costing
steps.text: Where the mobile app's job list comes from when someone clocks into a job: your T&A departments, your farms and units, farming departments, or your own custom list. Below it: the time at which a forgotten job is clocked out by itself.

steps.title: Payroll periods
steps.text: Payroll periods and locking are set up in Employee Master › Payroll Periods. It's the same list, and a locked period can no longer be changed.

steps.title: Teams
steps.text: Your active teams, and those you've deactivated. Search finds a team by its name, manager or members.

steps.title: Create a team
steps.text: Click + New Team: name the team, add its vehicle (for example the tractor or trailer it uses), choose the manager pay, then Save.

steps.title: How the manager is paid on team work
steps.text:
When a team is paid as a team, the quantity is shared among the workers who clocked in:
• Normal: the manager is paid for the team's full quantity; the workers share it.
• Equal share: the manager gets an equal share, like a worker.
• Average only: the manager gets the workers' average share.

steps.title: Your teams
steps.text: One row per team: its manager, members and manager pay. Click a row to add or remove people, choose the manager (the star) or change its settings.

steps.title: Data Tools
steps.text: Import Teams (names, vehicles, manager pay) and Import Members (Team + PIN) are separate files, each with its own template here. The exports use the same columns, so you can change one and import it again.

steps.title: Transfer Employee
steps.text: Move someone from one team to another in one step. The move is recorded in both teams' history.

steps.title: Two lists
steps.text: Piecework Activities are paid per unit. Job Costing Activities only record time. On each, Active | Deactivated switches between the activities in use and the ones switched off.

steps.title: Add Activity
steps.text: What people are paid for, the unit it's counted in (for example bins or trees), and the rate per unit for workers and for managers.

steps.title: Data Tools
steps.text: Download the import template, import many activities at once from Excel (names that are already there are skipped), or export them all to Excel. It works on the tab you are on.

steps.title: Each activity
steps.text: Its current worker and manager rate. Pricing Ledger keeps every rate with the date it started, so past days are paid at the rate that applied then. You can also edit or deactivate it.

steps.title: Job Costing Activities
steps.text: On this tab, Add Activity adds a job for the Job Costing clock on the mobile app, such as Irrigation or Maintenance. Time is recorded against it; it has no unit or rate.

steps.title: Create Task
steps.text: Give work to a team or a phone user: which activities and how much, on which farm and units, how they're paid, what evidence the phone must collect, and the dates.

steps.title: Active and completed
steps.text: Active tasks are pending or in progress. Completed tasks are finished. The search finds a task by its name, farm, unit, activity, tag or team.

steps.title: Each task
steps.text: What and where, who it is for, Individual or Team pay, the dates (with how many days overdue), and a progress bar of what has been captured against the target. Click a task to see its details and everything captured for it.

steps.title: From start to finish
steps.text: A task starts as Pending: you can still edit or delete it. Start puts it In Progress. Complete moves it to Completed Tasks once the work is done.

steps.title: Older and newer
steps.text: Move through the list, newest first.

steps.title: The day
steps.text: Pick the day, or step through days with the arrows. The grid reloads for the team you've chosen.

steps.title: The team
steps.text: Choose the team, then Load Grid. Each team's day is checked and committed on its own.

steps.title: Import Data and Import History
steps.text: In Data Tools: Import Data brings in production from an Excel sheet: you match its columns, it's validated, then imported. Import History lists past imports, and one can be rolled back if nothing in it has been committed.

steps.title: Export Excel
steps.text: In Data Tools: the grid on screen, as a spreadsheet.

steps.title: The grid
steps.text: One row per team member. Their shift and clockings from Time & Attendance, a column per task activity with their quantities and times, then their hours and wages: normal, approved and potential overtime, Sunday/public holiday, piece wage and the total. Time on a task is paid by quantity, so it comes off normal time.

steps.title: Check, then commit
steps.text:
Save Draft keeps your changes. Commit to Payroll makes the day final: its records lock. Unlock reopens committed records, and Revert Edits puts back what the phones captured.

If the day falls in a locked payroll period (Employee Master › Payroll Periods), it can't be saved, committed, unlocked or reverted until that period is unlocked. You'll see who and which dates are affected.

steps.title: Date range
steps.text: Choose the dates and click Load Data. Export saves what's on screen to Excel.

steps.title: The totals
steps.text:
Total hours, how many people and jobs, jobs still running, and flagged jobs.

A job is flagged when it ran over 14 hours or has no activity chosen. A job still running has no clock-out yet.

steps.title: Find what you need
steps.text: Search by name or PIN, choose a department, or click Flagged Only to see just the jobs that need checking.

steps.title: Jobs per person
steps.text: Click a person to open their jobs: the unit, the activity, when it started and ended, how long, and who captured it. To correct a time, type it into the clock-in or clock-out box and press Enter. Use Edit for another day, the unit or the activity on a job.

steps.title: Where the job list comes from
steps.text: The activities people clock into are the Job Costing Activities under Activities & Pricing. The departments or units come from the setting in Production Settings.

steps.title: Dates
steps.text: The date range for the report.

steps.title: Narrow it down
steps.text: Filters holds the department, team, task and employee choices, and how the rows are sorted. The number on the button shows how many filters are on. Leave them on All for everyone.

steps.title: Report Type
steps.text:
• Daily Detailed: each person's production per day.
• Employee Daily Evidence: the photos captured with it.
• Employee Summary and Activity Summary: totals for the date range, per person or per activity.
• Job Costing (by employee), Job Costing Summary (a matrix of people and jobs) and Job Costing Wages (hours × hourly rate per day; the Global Hourly Rate applies here when it's switched on).
• Global Summary: everything combined.

steps.title: Sort
steps.text: Sort by in Filters orders the rows by name, PIN or quantity. Tick Ignore letters in PIN sort to sort PINs by their numbers only.

steps.title: Generate Report
steps.text: Shows the report on screen. Export next to it saves it as an Excel spreadsheet.

steps.title: Which day
steps.text: Choose the day to show.

steps.title: Teams and tasks
steps.text: Teams and Tasks: tick the ones to show (nothing ticked shows them all). The map plots again when you close the list. The number shows how many you've ticked.

steps.title: Plot Activities
steps.text: Puts every capture on the map where it was made, over your farms and units. Click a pin to see who captured what, when, and any photo.

steps.title: Save Default View
steps.text: Move and zoom the map to your farms, then save it. The map opens there next time.
